instructions.title: How to use Markdown Table Generator

steps.title: Pick how to start
steps.description: Switch to the visual editor to build a table from scratch, or use 'Paste CSV / TSV / Markdown' to import existing data. The auto-detect delimiter handles comma, semicolon and tab inputs without extra config.

steps.title: Edit cells, rows and columns
steps.description: Type directly into header and body cells. Use the row controls to reorder, duplicate or delete rows, and the + button to append a new column. Empty cells stay empty in the Markdown output.

steps.title: Set column alignment
steps.description: Click the alignment icon on any column header to cycle through none, left, center and right. The separator row in the Markdown output updates automatically with `:---`, `:---:` and `---:` markers.

steps.title: Copy or preview the result
steps.description: Toggle 'Pretty padding' to align cells visually inside the Markdown source. Use the live preview to confirm rendering, then copy the Markdown to clipboard with one click.

features: Visual table editor with add/remove/reorder rows and columns
Paste CSV, TSV or existing Markdown table to import
Per-column left, center, right or no alignment
Round-trip parsing of existing GFM Markdown tables
Pretty-printed padded output that lines up visually
Compact output mode for minimal Markdown
Automatic escaping of pipes and newlines in cells
Live HTML preview of the rendered table
useCases: Document API responses or config schemas in README files
Convert spreadsheet exports into GitHub-ready Markdown tables
Draft comparison tables for blog posts and product pages
Edit a table that already lives inside a Markdown document
Build feature matrices for marketing or release notes
Turn CSV reports into shareable Markdown for chat or PRs
Keep static-site documentation tables in version control
Format data for Notion, Obsidian or Bear that supports GFM
proTips: Use 'Pretty padding' while editing — the aligned source is much easier to diff in pull requests
Pipes inside data are auto-escaped to `\|` so links and code samples stay intact
To re-edit an existing Markdown table, paste it into the import box and the editor will reload it with the original alignment

Newlines inside a cell become `
` so multi-line notes survive the GFM round-trip
Set sensible header names before importing CSV — they double as column identifiers in your final table
troubleshooting: If imported CSV columns look merged, set the delimiter explicitly instead of relying on auto-detect
Markdown tables without a `| --- |` separator row cannot be re-imported — add the separator and try again
If the live preview looks different from the Markdown, your renderer may not support GFM alignment markers
Very wide tables wrap horizontally on small screens — toggle 'Pretty padding' off to keep the source compact
Removing the last column resets the layout — use 'Example' to restore a working table quickly

pageDescription: Create clean Markdown tables without counting pipes. Use the visual editor to add rows, reorder columns and set per-column alignment, or paste CSV, TSV or an existing Markdown table to import data instantly. Pipes and newlines inside cells are escaped automatically so the output stays valid GitHub Flavored Markdown. Toggle pretty padding for a diff-friendly source, preview the rendered HTML live and copy the result with one click. Perfect for README files, blog posts, comparison pages and API documentation. Free, browser-based, no signup required.
